items.title: Pete Levin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001
items.q: Actually Alan Raph, who you interviewed, was in that [brass quintet]

ctx.x: Do you still play the horn?

Very little. I have it, but it’s not something you can not touch for six months and just pick up. For a little while I was playing in a brass quintet a few years ago, up here in Danbury, just with some friends. It was a very relaxed situation. Actually Alan Raph, who you interviewed, was in that, and a local trumpet player, Bucky Milan who I’ve known for years, he played with Urbie Green and Buddy Rich years ago and he’s mainly an artist nowadays, paints beautifully. This was a very informal quintet, playing…
be lobbying to — let’s stop and have a beer, let’s take a long break. Long answer to an easy question. So no, I don’t play much. You can’t, you really have to keep up with that.
